## Natural history notes

A small earth-boring scarab beetle characterized by its compact, rounded body, dark brown to black coloration, and strong digging legs. In Florida, it is found in sandy soils, pine flatwoods, scrub, sandhills, open woodlands, and other habitats where loose soil and underground fungi or organic matter are available. Adults spend much of their time underground and may come to lights at night, while the larvae develop in the soil and are thought to feed on buried fungi or decaying organic material.
